newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's All Corp to be liquidated by end-March - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan's All Corp to be liquidated by end-March - report.

text.p: Tokyo-based All Corp, a non-bank financial institution burdened by overlending in the "bubble" economy of the late 1980s, will be liquidated by the end of March, a Japanese financial daily reported on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that the non-bank was expected to make an official announcement by the end of this week.
Tokai Bank, All-Corp's major lender, is expected to support the liquidation, the financial daily said.
A former director of Tokai assumed the presidency of All Corp in 1992 but failed to recover its loans, the paper reported.

The non-bank will hold an extraordinary shareholder's meeting by the end of March to ask for approval for liquidation if Tokai Bank receives the approval of Sakura Bank and other related financial institutions.

Tokai Bank's outstanding loans to All Corp amounted to 61 billion yen ($521.4 million) at the end of March 1996, while Sakura Bank was owed 21 billion yen ($179 million) and Chuo Trust and Banking Co had 9.4 billion yen ($80.3 million) outstanding, the paper reported.
